lesson_title: The Candle Doing Both: Physical vs Chemical Change
hook_text: One candle flame is running TWO different kinds of change at once — millimetres apart.
clip_script: Look at a burning candle. Right now, millimetres apart, it is running the two great kinds of change in all of chemistry — at the same time. At the top: the flame's heat melts the wax into a clear pool. Tilt the candle, let a drop run down the side, and it cools back into hard wax. You can peel it off and remould it. Same substance, round trip complete — that is PHYSICAL change. Now the wick: the liquid wax climbing it meets the flame and burns — rebuilt, atom by atom, into carbon dioxide and water vapour that drift away invisibly. That wax is never coming back. No freezer un-burns anything — that is CHEMICAL change: new substances, one-way traffic. It is why the candle shrinks night after night: the melted wax returns, the burnt wax never does. And the whole topic is one question — is there a new substance? Ice tray: no, physical. Braai fire: yes, chemical. One question, asked at the top of the candle and again at the wick — and you can now classify any change in the universe.
visual_style: A single candle in the dark, macro shots: a glassy melt pool at the top with a drop hardening mid-run down the side, then the wick where wax streams upward and bursts into labelled molecules of carbon dioxide and water drifting away; split labels PHYSICAL and CHEMICAL glow on either side of the flame.
mood: Quiet close-up wonder — an ordinary object caught running the whole syllabus.
pacing: Slow candlelit open, crisp two-sided comparison, tightening rhythm to the one-question punchline.
